title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Bardo Tesserae. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. No image generation is available in this session, so the build is code-led either way.

options.label: Bardo Tesserae
options.lineage: Roman-African floor mosaics of the Bardo Museum, Tunis: limestone and basalt tesserae, an emblema panel at the centre, geometric border bands
options.thesis: A profile assembled from small, exact, verifiable units, the way a Tunis mosaic builds a whole picture from stone squares; it refuses the dark terminal-styled developer landing page with glowing skill cards.
materials: 2px grout gaps on an 8px tessera module
options.viewport: Left: name in Marcellus inscriptional capitals over the positioning statement in Public Sans, the availability line and two actions (LinkedIn, View CV). Right: the portrait set as the emblema, a square panel inside a hand-authored SVG tessera border. Above: a sticky nav strip that is itself a thin geometric border band; skills, when reached, are square tiles set tight in a grouted grid, backend tiles filled blue, growth tiles outlined, learning tiles hatched.
options.risk: Reads as museum or heritage costume if tesserae leak beyond the three places they belong (emblema border, skill tiles, section rules), and Roman capitals can feel pompous to a tech lead; type is set restrained to hold it.

raised.raise: Registration: every block, tile, rule and image snaps to one 8px module; nothing sits off-grid.
Type commitment: the scale takes real steps (display 3.5rem to body 1.0625rem, weight contrast obvious), never a timid hierarchy.
One grid is the entire composition: photo, tiles and columns are sized in module multiples.
Exactly one accent: smalti blue appears only on actions, the current nav item and core-skill tiles; nothing else is coloured.
Named states: skill tiles carry three distinct states (core / growing / learning) legible without colour, by fill, outline and hatch.
Courses: the experience timeline reads as stacked horizontal courses against a fixed date ruler, body measure held at 65 to 72ch.

options.label: API Reference
options.lineage: API reference documentation: the two-pane reference pages tech leads read every day
options.thesis: The profile written like the reference page for a well-designed service: a stable index, precise entries, code only where there is code.
materials: monospace reserved for real technology names
options.viewport: Top: a slim docs-style nav with section anchors and a search-less index. Below: name and one-line description as the page title block, the positioning statement as the summary, availability as a labelled field, then the first entries (Backend, Cloud) as reference blocks with tags rendered as code.
options.risk: Familiar by design; this is where most developer portfolios land, and it will look competent rather than memorable.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.lineage: kinetic tensegrity sculpture: carbon rods held apart by red cord
options.thesis: Skills drawn as a force network: Java backend as the compression core, cloud and AI as the tension members pulling it outward.
options.viewport: A single force diagram fills the first screen: the backend node at centre, cloud, DevOps and AI nodes held in tension around it, name and availability pinned to nodes with leader lines.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity: it literally draws the backend-core-growing-outward mechanism. Loses on audience identification: recruiters do not read force diagrams, and the red cord fights the calm brief.
options.risk: Reads as a data-viz demo rather than a person; the diagram must stay legible on a phone.

options.label: Edo Block Registration
options.lineage: Edo woodblock printing, one registered colour block at a time
options.thesis: The page prints itself in layers: keyline first, then each skill area drops its colour in.
options.viewport: A keyline-only page that fills with colour blocks as you scroll.
options.case: Layered reveal hides content from a one-minute reader; the Edo world does not belong to a recruiter.

options.label: Futurist Bolted Book
options.lineage: machine-bound futurist book, wood type at 15 to 45 degrees
options.thesis: Every section a typographic collision at engine speed.
options.viewport: Name in wood type slammed across the fold at 30 degrees.
options.case: Loud by definition; the brief forbids flashy, and rotated type destroys scan speed.
options.kept: A type scale that takes real steps.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.lineage: live scenes rendered as glyph density on a phosphor grid
options.thesis: The portrait and page rendered as a live character grid.
options.viewport: A glyph-rendered portrait beside a monospace column of facts.
options.case: The dark terminal is the category rut this brief rejects; novelty over credibility.
options.kept: One grid is the whole composition.

options.label: VU-Meter Bridge
options.lineage: a row of VU meters across a recording desk
options.thesis: Skills as a row of identical meters, needles leaning toward the red.
options.viewport: A meter bridge across the fold, one needle per skill area.
options.case: Audio instruments have no link to the audience; rating skills with needles overstates and gamifies.
options.kept: Exactly one accent colour, used once.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.lineage: a coiled clay tower built course by course
options.thesis: The career as ascending courses of clay.
options.viewport: Horizontal courses stacked to the fold, newest course on top.
options.case: Terracotta and umber fight the calm brief; recruiters do not identify with ceramics.
options.kept: Stacked courses with a fixed ruler and a held measure.
options.risk: Heavy and warm in the wrong way.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio recruiters already know: hero, skill cards, project cards, contact, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and a one-line tagline centred over a row of skill cards with icons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
